start.yourVideoIsOn: Your video is on the timeline. To have me work on what is said, transcribe it first (Transcribe, on the video below). Tell me what you want:
start.theFinalFormatLandscape: - the **final format** (landscape, vertical 9:16, square) and the target **length**;
start.whatToCutSilences: - what to **cut**: silences, hesitations, specific passages;
start.theStyleOfCaptions: - the **style** of captions and titles, the **words to highlight**;
start.iWillShowYou: I will show you each change as a preview before applying it.
start.sourcesAreIn: Your {n} sources are in the project. For me to read what is said in the videos and sounds, transcribe them first (Transcribe, on each one in the material). Here is how I will work:
start.sourcesReadAll: - I read **everything**: the documents page by page, the pictures, the videos and sounds with what is said;
start.sourcesBrief: - what I learn goes into the project's **brief**: subject, audience, key messages, figures, brand colours;
start.sourcesDirections: - then I propose **two or three directions** for the video (format, length, scene by scene), and make the one you choose.
start.sourcesSend: The analysis is ready below: send it as it is, or add what the video is for (where it will be shown, for whom, how long).
start.kitApplied: The project's kit (brief.json) is in: its colours and fonts are the project's, and its brief is the one I follow.

assistant.itReadsTheDocument: It reads the document, renders frames to check its work and, when needed, writes new nodes for the project. It never changes anything without your approval.
assistant.forClaudeTwoPaths: For Claude, two paths: the **local companion** (your Claude Code login, no key), or the server's key. The local models' address is set here too. The badge in the header shows which path is used.
assistant.claudeOpusForThe: Claude: Opus for the most careful work, Sonnet for a good balance, Haiku to go fast. The menu also offers the **OpenAI**, **Gemini** and **OpenRouter** models the server has a key for, and **local models** (Ollama, LM Studio). You can switch models during a conversation.
assistant.justWriteWhatYou: Just write what you want. "this", "this layer", "here" refer to the **selection** and the **current time**, shown under the field.
assistant.theMicrophoneWritesWhat: The microphone in a message box writes what you say where the cursor is, for you to read before sending. Click to speak, click to stop, **Escape** drops the recording. The first time, Tramme offers to download a speech model; where your voice is transcribed is a setting in Models.
assistant.keepWritingMessagesQueue: Keep writing: your messages wait above the box, each with a button to take it back, and leave together when the turn ends, each with the context of the moment it was written (the time, the selection). After a stop they stay, with a **Send now** button.
assistant.itsChangesArriveAs: Its changes arrive as a **proposal**: visible in the preview, to apply or decline. Once applied, they can be undone like any other change.
assistant.eachConversationStaysIn: Each conversation stays in the project. Reopen one to continue it; **+** starts another without erasing the previous ones.

drawn.anImageSequencePlays: An **image sequence** plays your drawings one after another, like a cartoon. You draw in your usual software, Tramme handles the rhythm.
drawn.dropThemHereTogether: Drop them here together, numbered in their names (eye_01.png, eye_02.png…). They go into a folder named after them.
drawn.rightClickOneOf: Right-click one of the drawings, **Animate the folder**: an Image sequence layer is created with all the drawings, in order.
drawn.hold2GivesThe:
**Hold**: 2 gives the anime rhythm "on twos" (each drawing held for two frames).
**Exposure sheet**: the order and length of each drawing, for example "1-4/2, 5/6, 4-1/2, x/3".
**Forced drawing**: pick the drawing with hold keyframes, for a mouth for example.
drawn.playWithSpaceThe: Play with **Space**. The preview shows exactly the export's frames, and motion blur never blends two drawings.

sound.libraryToolsLayersMix: The sound library, the sound tools, sound layers, the mix.
sound.everySoundIsA: Every sound is a file played by a **Sound** layer. Tramme ships a library of **421 recorded sounds** (impacts, interface, digital, jingles, sci-fi; free for any use) and **sounds written as code** (whoosh, riser, boom, sparkle…). The preview and every export mix them the same way.
sound.writeSoundDesignOr: Write **/sound-design**, or simply "a whoosh on each transition". The assistant searches the library, places each sound so its **hit lands on the frame**, writes the ones the library lacks, lowers the music under a voice and checks the mix. As always, it arrives as a proposal.
sound.typeSfxToSearch: **/sfx** searches the library ("metal hit", "riser", "click"), then places a sound **on** moments the video names: entrances, exits, markers, cuts, beats, bars. Also: **/synth** (a sound written as code), **/duck** (music under the voice), **/sound-keep** (keep a sound in your library, shared by your projects), **/generate-sound** (a sound effect, a music bed or a voice-over made by a provider, when the server has a key).
sound.theMicrophoneRecordsFrom: The microphone beside play records a voice-over from the playhead: a short count-in, headphones advised, a press ends it, **Escape** drops it. The take becomes a sound clip over a sound track, and what it covers is cut by it, never lost.
sound.itsBarStartsWhere: Its bar starts where the sound plays: move it, trim it like any layer. A sound placed several times alternates its variants, so it does not sound copied.
sound.volumeAnimateItFor:
**Volume**: animate it with keyframes for a fade or to lower the sound under a voice.
**Fade in**, **Fade out**: soft starts and ends.
**Low cut**, **High cut**: thinner, or muffled and far away.
**Reverb**: the sound in a room.
**Speed**: lower and longer under 1, higher and shorter over 1.
sound.playWithSpaceThe: Play with **Space**: you hear the mix of the export. **/check** also reads the sound: a mix that clips, one far too loud or too quiet, two sounds landing together.
sound.mp4AndWebmCarry: MP4 and WebM carry the sound; **WAV** gives the sound alone, to finish it elsewhere.

editor.theEditorSPanels: The editor's panels and what they are for.
editor.everythingYouDoHere: Everything you do here changes the project's document, saved automatically. Every action can be undone with **Ctrl+Z**.
editor.theSameEngineAs: The same engine as the export. Click a layer to select it, then move, rotate or scale it with the handles. **Ctrl+wheel** to zoom, **Space** drag to pan.
editor.thePreviewCanLighten: The preview can lighten during playback depending on your computer. Here, and in the settings, you choose how far. Exports always stay at full quality.
editor.dragToReorderOr: Drag to reorder or group, double-click to rename, right-click for the rest (duplicate, precompose, hide). The **+** button adds a layer: shape, text, image, drawing sequence, particles, shader…
editor.importImagesFontsSounds: Import images, fonts, sounds and videos by drag and drop. Numbered drawings (eye_01.png, eye_02.png…) imported together go into their own folder: right-click, **Animate the folder**.
editor.spaceToPlayOr: **Space** to play or stop, arrows to step frame by frame. The timecode can be edited directly (8.5 s, 255f…).
editor.moveOrTrimThe: Move or trim the layer bars, drag the keys to change their moment. The right click opens the timeline's menus: split a clip at the playhead, a marker, the curve of a key.
editor.valuesOverTimeWith: Values over time, with their Bézier handles. This is where you tune the rhythm of a motion.
editor.thePropertiesOfThe: The properties of the selected layer, or of the composition. Each can be **static**, **animated**, an **expression** or **linked** to another (⋯ button). Modifiers and effects stack here too.
editor.askForAChange: Ask for a change: it works on the selection and the current time, checks its work with rendered frames and **proposes** its changes. You see them in the preview, then apply or decline them.
editor.mp4WebmWithTransparency: MP4, WebM with transparency, GIF, PNG sequence, Lottie, SVG or sound. The file is saved to your computer or kept in the project.
editor.moreToursAreHere: More tours are in the help menu: the tricks, drawn animation, sound, looks, cutting on tracks, speech, the tools of the / menu, the assistant. Enjoy creating.

home.createOpenAndFind: Create, open and find your projects.
home.trammeIsAMotion:
Tramme makes motion design films from your words: you direct, it stages, builds and reviews. Every film stays a **document** you can open up and refine, in words or by hand.
This tour takes a minute.
home.mostRecentFirstWith: Most recent first, with their thumbnail. Each card's menu lets you rename, duplicate, save the .tramme archive to your computer or delete.
home.eachExampleBecomesYour: Each example becomes your own copy, which you can change freely.
home.themePreviewQualityFor: Theme, language, preview quality for your computer's power, access to the assistant. Shortcut: **Ctrl+,**
home.allGuidedToursAre: All guided tours are here, at any time. Another one awaits you the first time you open a project.
home.describeTheFilm: Describe the film you want, add its material (documents, pictures, footage, a whole folder), pick a format: the project opens in the studio with Tramme already at work. A blank project, a video or a file to open: **Other ways in**.

studio.title: Discover the studio
studio.summary: Direct the film in words: notes, scenes, takes.
studio.introBody:
Here you direct the film in words: Tramme stages it, builds it, reviews it. Nothing to operate.
This tour takes a minute.
studio.directBody: Say what you want, as you would to an editor: "the intro drags", "a bolder title here". **Enter** sends. **/** opens the tools and workflows.
studio.pinBody: A click on the picture pins your note there: it is about what shows at that moment. The pin (**P**) does the same.
studio.storyboardBody: Click a scene to put it in focus: your notes and the suggestions are about it. Drag to run through the film.
studio.notesBody: Each note gets a take: compare it with before, keep it, set it aside or ask for another. Everything can be undone.
studio.directionBody: What Tramme follows: the idea of the film, the brief (subject, tone, rules), the palette, the material. Correct it here: it wins over Tramme's habits.
studio.atelierBody: For the detail: layers, timeline, curves and inspector. The same project, seen up close.

tips.featuresThatDoNot: The features that do not jump out: timeline zoom, lasso, cuts, menus, fields, keyboard
tips.littleGesturesHidden: A few gestures hide in the panels. One pass, and the atelier holds no surprise any more.
tips.ctrlOrCmdAnd: **Ctrl** (or **Cmd**) and the wheel zoom the timeline around the pointer. Drag in an empty place to draw a lasso over clips and keyframes: **Shift** adds to the selection, **Ctrl** flips it.
tips.aClipsEdgesMagnetise: A clip's edges snap to the start and the end, the playhead, the markers and the other clips. Hold **Shift** to move freely.
tips.dragTheLeftEdge: Drag the left edge of a video, a sound or a composition: its head is cut off, what follows stays in place. The right edge cuts the tail.
tips.theCutInTheFile: **Cut in the file** shows the whole video and the part the layer plays. Slide the left handle to take the passage further in the file, the right one to lengthen or shorten it.
tips.thumbsAlongTheVideoClips: A video's clip shows its film: small thumbs decoded in the background, never while the film plays. The top corners of a video or a sound drag its **fade in** and **fade out**. The right click on a clip adds two tricks: a **crossfade** with the layer under it, and **loop the section to the end**.
tips.everyLineBetween: Every line between two panels drags: this one grows or shrinks the **chat**, the one over the timeline sets its height, the ones at the sides set the panels' width. Each remembers its size.
tips.theSpeedOfAVideo: A video has a **Speed** (0.25× to 4×): slower or faster, the pitch of its sound with it. Its section can also **loop** while the layer runs.
tips.rightClickTheTimeline: The timeline has its own menus. On a clip: **split**, cut the start or the end, or bring it **to the playhead**, then everything a layer can do. On an empty place or the ruler: the playhead or a **marker** there, end the composition there. On a keyframe: its curve.
tips.dragAPropertysLabel: Drag a property's name left and right to change its value. A field takes arithmetic: type **1920/2**, it is computed.
tips.theDotsOfAProperty: The diamond at the left of a property animates it (a keyframe at the playhead). The **...** at its right turn it into an expression, link it to another property or add a modifier (wiggle, loop).
tips.theMasksSectionAdds: The **Masks** section of the inspector adds a mask to a layer: a path that adds, subtracts or intersects. A mask can ride on an object followed by the **track** tool.
tips.theWheelZoomsThe: **Ctrl** and the wheel zoom the preview, the middle button (or **Space** held) pans it. The zoom menu brings it back to fit.
tips.safeZonesTheGrid: Beside the zoom, three buttons: the **safe zones** (the social vertical zone, or the broadcast action and title zones), a **grid** of thirds, and the **onion skin** for drawn animation: the previous drawing in red, the next in green, at rest.
tips.spacePlaysThe: **Space** plays, the arrows go one frame (with **Shift**, one second), **Home** and **End** go to the ends. **M** drops a marker, **1** to **9** jump to the markers. **Ctrl+D** duplicates, **Delete** removes.
tips.theTwoArrowsUndo: The two arrows undo and redo (**Ctrl+Z**, **Ctrl+Shift+Z**), the assistant's changes as well: their tooltip says what they undo.
tips.theClockBesideTheSaved: The clock beside the save state keeps **versions**: an instant of the project named with a date. Come back to one when a direction turned out wrong; add one before a big change.
tips.motionBlurFollowsThe: The motion blur follows the document's setting; the export can render it finer, or without blur for a quick check. When the content ends before the composition, the export offers to trim it.
tips.everythingElseExplains: Everything else explains itself: hover a control to read what it does. The other tours are under the help button.

speech.title: Speech and transcription
speech.summary: Transcribe what is said, for the captions and the assistant
speech.introBody: A sound or a video is never transcribed on its own: you decide. Once transcribed, its words are timed, ready for the captions and for the assistant, which can then cut silences or place a word at the moment it is said.
speech.materialBody: Each video and sound of the film has its **Transcribe** button here. It turns to **Transcribed** once done.
speech.inspectorBody: A sound or video layer has a **Speech** section: transcribe it, or again after a change of file.
speech.assetsBody: The sounds and videos of the project show their state here, with the button; the right click offers it too.
speech.filesBody: A sound or a video joined to a message carries the same button. When the assistant needs the words of a media not transcribed yet, it asks you first.
speech.wordsBody: Ask for captions, cuts of the silences and hesitations, or a keyword when it is said: the assistant works on the transcript.

tours.montage.title: Cut a film on tracks
tours.montage.summary: Lanes, the keys that cut, moving a cut, cameras, adjustment clips, chapters, the media, the mixer, publishing.
tours.montage.welcomeBody: A sequence lays its clips on tracks, one after another, the way an editor does. The film is still the same document: nothing here changes how it renders. The right click on an empty place of the timeline lays the layers out on tracks.
tours.montage.lanesBody: Each track has its header: its name (double click), the magnet that makes the clips close their gaps by themselves, the eye, the sound, solo, and the lock that keeps a track from being touched. A clip dropped on another lane changes track.
tours.montage.keysBody: **Ctrl+B** cuts at the playhead. **Q** and **W** trim the start and the end of the selected clips to it. **Shift+Delete** removes and closes the gap (Delete does as much on a magnetic track). **Ctrl+C**, **Ctrl+V** and **Ctrl+Alt+V** copy, paste and paste the look. **L** links clips, **Ctrl+Shift+L** frees them. **,** inserts the media chosen in the panel at the playhead, **.** lays it over.
tours.montage.gesturesBody: Drag the edge of a clip with **Shift** to roll the cut between two shots. **Alt** and drag a clip slips what it shows in its file; **Ctrl+Alt** slides it between its neighbours. Right click a clip to detach its sound, line it up with another by sound, cut between cameras or match its look.
tours.montage.camerasBody: Select two videos of the same scene and right click: **Cut between these cameras**. They are lined up by their sound, each camera goes on its own track, and a panel cuts between them: press a camera's button, or **Alt** and its number, while the film plays or not. The cuts are plain clips, free to move afterwards.
tours.montage.adjustmentBody: Right click a lane's header, or its add button: **Add an adjustment clip at the playhead**. Its effects reach every track under it, for its length only: one look over several shots, without touching them.
tours.montage.chaptersBody: Right click a marker: **Make it a chapter**. Chapters are written into the files the command line renders, and **Copy the chapters as a list** (right click on an empty place of the timeline) gives the list as text.
tours.montage.mediaBody: Drag a medium onto a lane: it is inserted on a magnetic track, laid over elsewhere (**Alt** does the other). Bins and tags sort the media, the search finds a name or a word said in a clip. The source monitor sets an in and an out (**I**, **O**) and keeps the part as a sub-clip. A medium whose file went missing says so and can be found again.
tours.montage.mixerBody: One strip per sound track and bus: the fader, the pan, mute, solo, the bus it feeds. Arm **W** and move a fader while the film plays: the moves are written as the volume's automation. The master shows the loudness aimed at and measures the mix. The Mixer tab appears as soon as the film has a sound track.
tours.montage.publishBody: Pick where the film is going: what stands between it and that place is listed, each with its fix. **I** and **O** mark the part to export; several exports can wait in line while you go on editing.
tours.look.title: Grade and match a look
tours.look.summary: The scopes, matching one shot to another, the export.
tours.look.introBody: Colour is measured, not guessed: the scopes read the frame, colour wheels set it, and one shot can borrow the look of another.
tours.look.scopesBody: Select a layer that has a grading effect (a LUT, curves, wheels, a colour correction, a key): the **waveform** and the **vectorscope** of the frame appear beside the picture and follow it while you set the effect.
tours.look.matchBody: Select two or more videos or pictures and right click one: **Match the look of the first selected clip**. The others get colour wheels set to reproduce it, and the wheels stay yours to edit. **Ctrl+Alt+V** pastes a copied clip's attributes (effects, masks, speed) onto others.
tours.look.exportBody: On a video, the export panel offers **10 bits** where this browser's encoder has them, which keeps smooth gradients from banding. HDR waits for the browsers: the panel says so when it cannot be done.
tours.yours.title: Make it yours
tours.yours.summary: Tokens, plugins, packs and the tours they bring.
tours.yours.tokensBody: Brand colours and named curves, kept in the project. **+** adds a colour, a click on its swatch edits it. A property can point at a token by its name, **@name**: change the token once and everything that uses it follows.
tours.yours.pluginsBody: In the settings, **Plugins** are installed once and offered in every project: their tools (in the **/** menu), nodes and checks. The packs that ship with the editor are plugins too: charts, kinetic type, physics…
tours.yours.toursBody: A plugin can bring its own tour: it joins this menu, with the plugin's name beside it, as long as the project uses it. The tours seen are remembered, and the menu can offer them all again.
tours.tools.title: The tools of the / menu
tours.tools.summary: Footage, voice, the material read, whole motion pieces, following an object, pictures made, reuse, checks.
tours.tools.introBody: Type **/** in the message box: the tools and workflows list. The assistant uses the same ones. A tool that reads a video or a sound runs **once**, here, and saves what it found as a file of the project: the render only reads it, so the film stays exact.
tours.tools.footageBody: **/stabilize** takes the shake out of a video (or locks the shot), **/cutout** cuts the subject out so a title can pass behind it, **/depth** reads the depth for a parallax, **/skin** smooths faces, **/proxy** makes a lighter copy to edit smoothly (the exports read the original), **/upscale** enlarges a picture or a video to twice its size, **/interpolate** smooths a slow motion.
tours.tools.voiceBody: **/denoise** takes the background noise out of a voice. **/fillers** cuts the "uh"s and "um"s, and you can review them from the media panel and put each one back. **/shorts** cuts a long talking video into shorts: each is its own composition, framed to the format, captioned and titled.
tours.tools.materialBody: **/sources** reads what you joined (pictures, footage, sounds, PDF and markdown documents). **/beats** finds the tempo, the beats and the sections of a music, **/shots** the shots of a video, **/subjects** the people, **/palette** the colours of a picture. **/brief** keeps the project brief and **/kit** applies a style kit.
tours.tools.piecesTitle: A whole piece in one move
tours.tools.piecesBody: **/kinetic-title**, **/bar-chart**, **/stat**, **/quote**, **/logo-reveal**, **/list**, **/timeline**, **/split-screen**, **/map-journey** and **/transition** lay out a whole animated piece as ordinary layers and keyframes, editable afterwards. They read the style kit, so a film keeps one motion language.
tours.tools.followBody: **/track** follows something filmed (framed by a rectangle, or named) and **/callout** puts brackets and a label that stay on it. **/events** writes a list of events once, and **/event-counter**, **/event-tags** and **/event-receipt** all read it: change the list and they follow. **/svg-paths** turns an SVG into paths.
tours.tools.madeTitle: Pictures and clips made by a provider
tours.tools.madeBody: **/generate-image** and **/generate-video** have a picture or a clip made by a provider; the provider is chosen in the settings, Pictures and Videos. Each one is billed, so Tramme asks you first. The result is saved in the project and shown to the assistant so it can judge it.
tours.tools.reuseBody: **/block-add** saves a dressed selection as a block of the project and **/block-use** places it again, anywhere. **/component-keep**, **/component-use**, **/instantiate** and **/detach** work with components, a piece with parameters placed as many times as needed. **/library-add** and **/library-use** keep a plugin to share between projects.
tours.tools.checkBody: **/check** runs the quality checks and gives a contact sheet of the moments that matter. **/motion** shows a strip of frames to judge a movement. The assistant runs both before it sums up.

assistant.startOllamaOrLm: Start Ollama (or LM Studio with its local server), download a model that can use tools, then pick it in the model menu.

assistant.theLocalCompanionIs: The local companion is running and waiting for its token.
assistant.inTheCompanionS: In the companion's terminal, copy the "pairing token" line and paste it here. You only do this once in this browser.
assistant.itRunsClaudeWith: It runs the agent installed on this computer (Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity) with your own login, no key needed. Start it in the Tramme folder:
assistant.itConnectsToThisEditor: It connects to this editor on its own.

assistant.queueWaitsTurn: They leave together when the turn ends.
assistant.queueWaitsDecision: They leave once you apply or reject the proposal.
assistant.queueStopped: The turn stopped: they are still waiting.
assistant.commandHint: Runs right away. Or write what you want after the command, and the assistant does it.

settings.effortNone: This model has no effort levels.
settings.notifyDone: Tell me when the assistant is done
settings.resume: Go on after a network failure
settings.resumeHint: A task cut by the network or a busy server starts again by itself, waiting longer each time (2 s to 1 min, 6 attempts). Never after a used-up quota or a refused key.
settings.scenesApartHint: A film of three scenes or more is built scene by scene, each in a fresh context that keeps only the plan and the document, then assembled. It keeps the cost of a scene flat in a long film.

settings.aboutHint: The version of the app and its updates.

settings.areaConfirmHint: After you draw round layers or across them in the studio, the layers it proposes are shown for you to confirm. Choose when.

settings.notifyHint: A notification from the system when the editor is in the background (the browser asks once), a message in the editor after a long task.

chips.reviewWords: Watch the whole film as an art director would and fix what matters most: readability, rhythm, hierarchy, the transitions.
chips.paceWords: Give the film more rhythm: shorten the scenes that drag, sharper entrances, cuts on the beat, without changing the message.
chips.paletteWords: Propose another palette for the film, in keeping with its subject and tone, and apply it everywhere.
chips.soundWords: Work on the sound of the film: a bed that fits the tone, effects on the moments that matter, levels balanced.
chips.verticalWords: Make a vertical 9:16 version of the film for social media, in a new composition, each scene recomposed for the format.
chips.impactWords: Make this scene hit harder: a franker entrance, more contrast, a clearer hierarchy.
chips.calmerWords: Make this scene calmer: fewer things moving, softer moves, more air around the words.
chips.layoutWords: Recompose this scene differently: another layout and another camera move, the same message.
chips.shorterWords: Shorten this scene by about a third without losing its message, and move what follows.
